clue.text: In very cold environment have cereal for energy

indicators.note: the cold word forms the surroundings, so the cereal sits inside it

parts.note: cold means icy
bran is a cereal product

explanation.surface: Advice to eat breakfast cereal in a freezing climate to keep your strength up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' is the containment signal: the cold word surrounds the cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrancy is liveliness or vigour, a close synonym of energy.

clue.text: Making solemn pledges, revolutionary government secures victory

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the turned word holds the victory word inside
revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: GOV is a short form of government
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: A newly installed rebel regime wins and swears its oaths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a description of the regime but signals turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Vowing is promising solemnly, the same act as making pledges.

clue.text: Report what has been learnt about a city in India

indicators.note: about means around, so the report and learning words go round the a

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, a bang
lore is accumulated knowledge, what has been learnt

explanation.surface: Someone is describing what they found out on a visit to an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a gunshot noise here, not an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore (now Bengaluru) is a large city in southern India.

clue.text: Really try, taking part in a motorcycle event

indicators.note: the try word joins in, standing inside the motorcycle event letters

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races
to try a case in court is to hear it

explanation.surface: Really having a go at entering a motorbike race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is the judge's sense, to hear a case; the TT is the famous Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally or in reality, so it can replace really.

clue.text: Rib actor forgetting his last part

indicators.note: the actor word loses its final letter, with a theatrical pun on a forgotten part

parts.note: a co-star is a fellow actor

explanation.surface: An actor drying on stage and forgetting the end of his role, or being teased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rib' looks like a verb meaning tease; it is the anatomical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is the Latin and anatomical term for a rib.

clue.text: Palace in cathedral city, bishop's responsibility

parts.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
a see is the diocese a bishop is responsible for

explanation.surface: A palace in a cathedral city falls under the bishop's care, like a bishop's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee Palace in Paris is the official residence of the French president.

clue.text: Girl has turned out quite generous

indicators.note: to turn out is to be rearranged into something else, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A girl has grown up to be rather open-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges GIRL and HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Largish means fairly large, and large can mean generous or liberal.

clue.text: Capital of island protected by South Africa

indicators.note: protection surrounds, so the South Africa letters go round the rest

explanation.surface: An island's capital is under South African protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is not a link word here: it supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Church service gone wrong? Archdeacon's intervening

indicators.note: the archdeacon's letters come between the shuffled ones
going wrong means being disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A church service has gone badly and an archdeacon steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges gone into EONG; an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, Ven for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of the Anglican Church.

clue.text: Rotten fish served up during depression

indicators.note: the fish comes in the middle of the depression word

parts.note: a dent is a depression in a surface

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the dace is a small freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A rotten fish is served up in hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the fish into ECAD; 'depression' is a hollow, not low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decay, so rotten in the sense of corrupt fits.

clue.text: Following brief scare on Western Isles, loathe emptying weapon

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the scare word follows the isles

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island, so inches are isles

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the scare word loses its final letter

parts.note: to scare is to terrify

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: After a fright in the Hebrides, someone who hates guns is disarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island. 'brief' cuts TERRIFY to TERRIF, and 'emptying' leaves LE from loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester rifle is a famous repeating lever-action firearm, so a weapon.

clue.text: At close, market some may say falls

indicators.note: this flags that the words are spoken, and only some speakers would make them sound alike

parts.note: nigh means close or near; the agora was the market place of an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: At the end of trading, some say the market falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some may say' signals sound: NIGH AGORA spoken matches the falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, so the plural falls fits.

clue.text: Manila's wild beasts

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run in a new order

explanation.surface: The wild creatures of Manila, the Philippine capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges MANILAS; here the possessive S is a letter used.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals and beasts are synonyms for creatures.

clue.text: Maybe laptop displays menu after opening, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so their sound counts rather than their spelling

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin and a table is a list such as a menu; with the menu word after, they make pore table

explanation.surface: A laptop shows its menu after starting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals sound: PORE TABLE spoken is the answer. 'Maybe' marks the laptop as an example; 'displays' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a computer that can be carried about, an example of the category.

clue.text: Sports event taking old boy back a bit

indicators.note: back means the old boy letters are written backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a trace is a small bit

explanation.surface: A sports event takes a former pupil back a little way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames, so old boys belong here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is a famous annual rowing contest, an example of a sports event.

clue.text: Confine ambassador a short while

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE
min, short for minute, is a short while

explanation.surface: An ambassador is detained briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To hem in is to surround and restrict, so to confine.

clue.text: Wrongly advise teacher to finish early in class

indicators.note: finishing early cuts the teacher word short by its last letter

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a female teacher
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A teacher is told wrongly to finish the lesson early.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class is a form, and pupils call a female teacher Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform is to give someone wrong information, to advise wrongly.

clue.text: Work in vile prison

indicators.note: in means the work word goes inside the vile word

parts.note: base means low and vile
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: Doing hard labour in a filthy jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is farm work: tilling the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress prison stormed in 1789.

clue.text: Master likely to keep in lower classes

indicators.note: keeping something in holds it inside, so the likely word contains the classes

parts.note: apt means likely, as in apt to happen
D and E are the lowest of the UK social grades used in market research

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster tends to keep the lower forms in after school.
explanation.walkthrough: UK market research ranks social classes A to E, so DE are the lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is an expert, so a master of some skill.

clue.text: Tax cuts heartily accepted by family

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the family word holds the other letters

parts.note: a tribe is an extended family group

indicators.note: heartily means only the heart of the word, its middle letters

explanation.surface: Tax cuts are warmly welcomed by the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' reads as enthusiasm but asks for the heart of cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute was historically a payment or levy, so a tax.

clue.text: Cinema fire — temperature's hot inside

indicators.note: inside means the temperature and hot letters go within the fire word

parts.note: to fire someone up is to arouse them
T is the abbreviation for temperature
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A fire at the cinema, with the heat building up inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' is the verb meaning excite, AROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An art house is a cinema showing independent or foreign films.

clue.text: In theory, propane is explosive

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A safety warning that propane gas can explode, at least theoretically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is explosive' rearranges PROPANE.
explanation.definitionFit: On paper means as planned or theoretically, but not yet tested in practice.

clue.text: Stopped recording facility being installed

indicators.note: installing puts the facility word in place within the recording letters

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording
facility means ease, as in doing something with ease

explanation.surface: Work stopped while a recording studio was being fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' means skill or ease, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased means came to an end, the same as stopped.

clue.text: Food that is served by restaurant for starters, not so tasty

parts.note: tack is slang for food, as in hard tack
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: starters are the first course, so only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Food served first at a restaurant was not very good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tasty' is used in its sense of tasteful, so its opposite is more tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackier means more tasteless or vulgar, so less tasteful in style.

clue.text: Old aeroplane's constant measure of speed

parts.note: c is the constant for the speed of light
a rate is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: An old plane holds a steady speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constant' gives C, the physicists' symbol for the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for an old, ramshackle aircraft or car.

clue.text: Stretch of river steamer's stuck in?

indicators.note: the steamer word is stuck inside the river word

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a steamer is a cooking pan, and the possessive gives an S

explanation.surface: A stretch of river where a paddle steamer has run aground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamer' is a kitchen pan, not a boat; the Exe is a Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide area or stretch, of water or land.

clue.text: Cancel Caesarean section, if laid up

indicators.note: in a down clue, laid up means put upward, so the letters read backwards
a section is a piece cut from within the word

explanation.surface: A Caesarean operation is called off if the patient is bedridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' takes ESARE from inside Caesarean, and 'laid up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete, so to cancel.

clue.text: Top players lose in a cup game, collapsing about end of match

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the last letter of match
collapsing means falling apart, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The leading team crash out of a cup tie, collapsing late in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' rearranges LOSE IN A CUP GAME, and 'about' wraps it round H from 'end of match'.
explanation.definitionFit: The league champions are the side that won the league, the top players.

clue.text: City's name not included in old register

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: the name letter is left out of the register word

parts.note: to register is to enter, as in a record

explanation.surface: A city's name is missing from an ancient record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'register' is the verb, to enter in a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the county city of Devon, in south-west England.

clue.text: Soiled book, say, with old verses by Donne at the beginning

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here
rime is an old spelling of rhyme, as in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner

indicators.note: the beginning of the poet's name is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grubby book of old poems by John Donne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives EG, and RIME is the archaic form of rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Begrimed means covered in grime, so dirty and soiled.
